text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed lower but off the lows as trade selling countered the speculative buying and industry interest on the dips. July lost $27 to close at $1,823 per tonne. September gave up $5 to close at $1,860 per tonne. Traders said origins, particularly from Indonesia, were noticeably absent. This prompted talk that the Indonesian crop could be considerably lower than most had expected. It was added that some Indonesian exporters are apparently struggling to cover their commitments and that this could give rise to problems of contract defaults.

Arabica futures in New York ended broadly higher in choppy trade. Much of the day's focus centered on adjusting positions ahead of spot July's month-long delivery period scheduled to begin on June 20. As of June 18, July open interest stood at 2,638 lots, down 1,216 lots from the previous session. Meanwhile, CSCE certified coffee stocks stood at 47,286 60-kg bags as of June 17 or the equivalent of some 168 lots. There were another 1,500 bags pending grading, the Exchange reported.

UNITED STATES - The United States imported 1.294 million bags of coffee in April 1997, 26 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 7.698 million bags, which compares to 7.108 million bags the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose to 19.4 million bags, up from 17.1 million bags imported in 1995.

COSTA RICA - Following the June flower account, Costa Rica estimates its 1997/98 coffee crop will be 2.607 million 60-kg bags. It was added that the upcoming harvest will be slightly larger than the 2.223 million bags harvested last year. However, only recently the Costa Rican Coffee Institute said that the 1996/97 coffee campaign ended with a crop of 2.7 million 60-kg bags, similar to the last cycle.

PORTUGAL - Portugal imported 47,042 bags of coffee in February 1997, 14 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 101,000 bags, 11 per cent less than was imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 16 per cent to 727,000 bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/February 1997 were Ivory Coast (12,900 vs 17,600 bags), Uganda (12,800 vs 10,500 bags) and Brazil (17,600 vs 19,500 bags).
